title: Analog-to-Digital Conversion (ADC) & DAC: Successive Approximation (SAR), Sampling Times & Nyquist Limits
goal: Digitize physical reality: master 12-bit Successive Approximation Register (SAR) ADCs and DACs. Calculate input impedance RC sampling times, conversion clock budgets, Nyquist-Shannon sampling limits, multi-channel scan sequences, and internal VREFINT reference calibration.
recap: Yesterday, we controlled hardware timers and PWM generation. Today, we interface with the physical world by converting continuous analog voltages into quantized digital values using high-speed SAR ADCs.

parts.title: Physics of the 12-Bit Successive Approximation Register (SAR) ADC: Binary Search & DAC Comparator
say: The Successive Approximation Register (SAR) ADC is the workhorse analog converter in embedded microcontrollers, balancing high speed (1–3 megasamples per second) with 12-bit resolution.
A SAR ADC operates by executing a hardware binary search: it starts by testing the Most Significant Bit (MSB, Bit 11), generating half the reference voltage (VREF / 2) via an internal capacitive DAC.
A high-precision analog comparator compares the input voltage on the sample-and-hold capacitor against the internal DAC output.
If the input voltage exceeds the DAC voltage, the comparator output is 1, and Bit 11 is retained as 1; if less, Bit 11 is cleared to 0.
The SAR engine repeats this comparison for each subsequent bit (Bit 10 down to Bit 0) over exactly 12 successive clock cycles.
At 12-bit resolution, an input voltage between 0.0V and 3.3V is quantized into 4,096 discrete steps, yielding a resolution of 3.3V / 4096 = 0.805 millivolts per LSB.
parts.example: SAR conversion is like a balance scale where a merchant finds the exact weight of flour by testing standard brass weights (8oz, 4oz, 2oz, 1oz), keeping the weight if the scale doesn't tip and discarding it if it does.
parts.output:
12-Bit SAR ADC Conversion Model (VREF = 3.3V):
  LSB Resolution: 0.8057 mV
  Input Voltage:  1.6500 V
  Raw ADC Code:   0x800 (2048 / 4095)
  Reconstructed:  1.6500 V

codeNotes.note: Simulates 12-step binary search comparator evaluation from bit 11 down to 0
Calculates 1 LSB voltage quantum as VREF / 4096 (0.8057 mV)
1.65V input maps cleanly to midpoint code 0x800 (2048)

parts.tryIt: Pass an input of 3.3V and verify that the output clamps to 4095 (0xFFF).

check.question: How many clock cycles does a 12-bit SAR ADC take to execute the approximation phase after sampling completes?
options: Exactly 12 clock cycles (one cycle per bit of resolution)
4096 clock cycles
1 clock cycle
64 clock cycles
check.why: A Successive Approximation Register tests exactly one bit per clock cycle, requiring 12 cycles for 12-bit resolution.

parts.title: Sample-and-Hold Capacitor Charging & Input Impedance RC Sampling Times Invariant
say: Before a SAR ADC can convert a voltage, it must capture the physical electrical charge onto an internal sample-and-hold capacitor (typically C_adc = 4 pF to 8 pF).
During the sampling phase, an internal analog switch with resistance R_adc (approx 1 kOhm to 6 kOhm) closes, connecting the external sensor circuit to C_adc.
If the external sensor has an output impedance R_source (such as a 100 kOhm thermistor or resistive divider), an RC low-pass filter is formed with time constant tau = (R_source + R_adc) * C_adc.
To achieve 12-bit accuracy (1/4096 error = 0.024%), the capacitor must charge for at least ln(4096) = 8.32 time constants (typically 9 to 10 tau for margin).

Crucial Invariant: If firmware configures the sampling time register ('ADC_SMPR') too short, the capacitor will not finish charging, causing massive measurement errors and cross-talk between channels.
When measuring high-impedance sensors, engineers must either increase the ADC sampling cycles or insert an external operational amplifier voltage follower.
parts.example: Trying to fill a bucket from a garden hose: if the hose is thick (low impedance), the bucket fills in 2 seconds; if the hose has a narrow pinhole (high impedance), turning the valve off after 2 seconds leaves the bucket half empty.
parts.output:
ADC Sampling Time & Impedance Calculation:
  RC Time Constant (tau): 336.00 ns
  Min Sampling Time (9 tau): 3024.00 ns
  Clock Cycle Period: 71.43 ns
  Required ADC Sampling Cycles: 43 cycles

codeNotes.note: Calculates RC time constant tau = (R_source + R_adc) * C_adc
Enforces 9 time constants for settling within 1/2 LSB at 12-bit resolution
Shows that a 50k sensor requires at least 43 sampling cycles (e.g. SMPR=55.5 cycles)

parts.tryIt: Increase R_source to 100 kOhm and observe how the required sampling cycles rise to over 80 cycles.

check.question: Why does measuring a high-impedance (e.g. 100 kOhm) sensor with the minimum ADC sampling time (e.g. 3 cycles) produce incorrect readings?
options: The internal sample-and-hold capacitor does not have enough time to charge to the true sensor voltage
The ADC burns out from over-current
The high impedance causes the CPU clock to halt
The ADC automatically switches to 8-bit mode
check.why: High source impedance increases the RC charging time constant; if sampling time is shorter than ~9 tau, the internal capacitor is sampled before it reaches the true input voltage.

parts.title: ADC Clock Prescalers, Total Conversion Time & Nyquist Limits
say: The total conversion time of an analog channel is the sum of the sampling time and the approximation time: T_conv = T_sample + 12 cycles.
For example, with a sampling time of 15 cycles on a 14 MHz ADC clock, T_conv = 15 + 12 = 27 cycles, which takes 27 / 14,000,000 = 1.93 microseconds per conversion.
This corresponds to a maximum sampling rate of F_sample = 1 / 1.93 us = 518.5 kilosamples per second (ksps).

According to the Nyquist-Shannon Sampling Theorem, the maximum analog signal frequency that can be accurately reconstructed without aliasing is strictly less than half the sampling frequency: F_max < F_sample / 2.

If firmware attempts to sample a 40 kHz audio signal at a sample rate of 50 ksps (where Nyquist is 25 kHz), the high-frequency components alias into false low frequencies, corrupting the digital data.
An analog anti-aliasing low-pass RC filter must always precede the ADC pin to eliminate frequencies above the Nyquist limit.
parts.example: Nyquist aliasing is like watching car wheels in a movie appear to spin backwards because the camera's frame rate (24 fps) is too slow to capture the rapid rotation.
parts.output:
ADC Conversion Timing & Nyquist Limits:
  ADC Clock:       14.00 MHz
  Total Cycles:    27 (Sample=15 + SAR=12)
  Conversion Time: 1.93 microseconds
  Max Sample Rate: 518.52 ksps
  Nyquist Limit:   259.26 kHz (Max safe input bandwidth)

codeNotes.note: Total conversion cycles equals sampling cycles plus 12 SAR approximation cycles
Max sampling rate equals 1 / T_conv (518.52 ksps)
Nyquist limit is strictly half the sampling rate (259.26 kHz)

parts.tryIt: Recalculate conversion time when samplingCycles is set to 84 cycles for measuring a battery sensor.

check.question: According to the Nyquist-Shannon Sampling Theorem, what is the maximum signal frequency an ADC can digitize without aliasing at 100 ksps?
options: 50 kHz (strictly less than half the sample rate)
100 kHz (equal to the sample rate)
200 kHz (twice the sample rate)
10 kHz (one tenth of the sample rate)
check.why: The Nyquist criterion states that the sampling rate must exceed twice the highest frequency component of the analog signal (F_sample > 2 * F_signal), so F_max < 50 kHz at 100 ksps.

parts.title: Multi-Channel Regular vs Injected Sequences, End-of-Conversion (EOC) Flags & Overrun Detection
say: Embedded microcontrollers rarely measure just one analog pin; they monitor temperature, motor current, battery voltage, and joystick axes in a round-robin sequence.
The ADC Regular Channel Sequence Registers ('ADC_SQR1' to 'ADC_SQR3') define an ordered list of up to 16 channels to be converted automatically.
Additionally, advanced microcontrollers feature an Injected Channel Group ('ADC_JSQR').

An injected conversion acts like an interrupt for the ADC: if an injected trigger fires (such as a motor emergency over-current trigger), the ADC pauses the regular sequence, converts the high-priority injected channel immediately, and then resumes the regular sequence.
At the end of each channel conversion, the End of Conversion ('ADC_SR_EOC') flag is asserted.

If the CPU or DMA engine fails to read the data register ('ADC_DR') before the next conversion finishes, the Overrun flag ('ADC_SR_OVR') is set, alerting firmware that analog data was permanently lost.
parts.example: Regular channels are like customers standing in the grocery store checkout line; an injected channel is an emergency doctor walking in with an urgent pharmacy prescription who gets served immediately ahead of the line.
parts.output: [ADC EOC] Channel 0 converted: 2048 raw\n[ADC EOC] Channel 1 converted: 4095 raw

codeNotes.note: Configures ordered multi-channel scan sequence in ADC_SQR registers
Detects ADC_SR_OVR overrun if new conversion completes before DR is read
Reading ADC_DR automatically clears EOC flag for next conversion

parts.tryIt: Simulate calling stepConversion twice without calling readDataRegister and observe the overrun warning fire.

check.question: What is the key functional difference between Regular and Injected ADC channel groups in Cortex-M microcontrollers?
options: Injected conversions have higher priority and can interrupt an active regular sequence upon a hardware trigger
Regular channels operate only in 8-bit mode, while injected channels are 16-bit
Injected channels cannot generate interrupts
Regular channels require external power, while injected channels do not
check.why: Injected channels are designed for time-critical events (like motor current sampling during PWM center pulses); they interrupt regular background scanning immediately.

parts.title: Internal Voltage References (V_REFINT), Temperature Sensor Channels & Continuous Conversion Scanning
say: Microcontrollers operating on battery power experience power supply fluctuations: as a lithium battery discharges from 4.2V down to 3.0V, the ADC reference voltage VDDA drops.
If VDDA drops, naive raw ADC measurements become inaccurate because the LSB voltage changes.
To solve this, ARM microcontrollers integrate an ultra-stable, factory-calibrated internal reference voltage channel: 'V_REFINT' (typically 1.20V to 1.22V), connected internally to ADC Channel 17.
The factory measures V_REFINT at exactly 3.3V during silicon wafer manufacturing and writes the calibration code into read-only system memory ('VREFINT_CAL' at 0x1FFF7A2A).
By measuring the raw V_REFINT channel at runtime, firmware can back-calculate the exact live supply voltage VDDA using: VDDA = 3.3V * (VREFINT_CAL / Raw_VREFINT).
Additionally, an internal silicon Temperature Sensor channel ('ADC_IN16') allows monitoring microcontroller junction temperature to prevent thermal runaway.
parts.example: V_REFINT is like carrying a standard platinum 1-meter ruler in your toolbox: even if your plastic measuring tape expands in the heat, you can compare it against the platinum ruler to calibrate your measurements.
parts.output:
Runtime VREFINT Power Supply Calibration:
  Factory VREFINT_CAL (at 3.3V): 1500
  Live Raw VREFINT Reading:     1650
  Calculated Live VDDA Supply:   3.000 V (Battery has discharged!)
  Calibrated Sensor Reading:     1.500 V

codeNotes.note: Calculates true live VDDA by comparing raw VREFINT against factory calibration constant
Demonstrates detection of battery voltage droop from 3.3V down to 3.0V
Calibrates sensor voltage against the true dynamic VDDA value rather than assuming 3.3V

parts.tryIt: Pass a live_raw_vref of 1500 and verify that VDDA calculates to exactly 3.300 V.

check.question: Why is the internal V_REFINT channel essential for battery-powered IoT devices?
options: It allows firmware to determine the exact live VDDA supply voltage and calibrate all analog readings as the battery discharges
It acts as a physical solar charger for the battery
It boosts the battery voltage back up to 5V
It prevents the microcontroller from waking up
check.why: As a battery discharges, the ADC reference voltage drops; measuring the fixed internal bandgap V_REFINT allows firmware to calculate the exact real-time supply voltage and prevent false readings.

summary: A 12-bit SAR ADC executes a 12-clock binary search comparing analog input against internal capacitive DAC voltages, providing 0.805 mV resolution at 3.3V.
Input impedance dictates sampling time: external source resistance and internal capacitance form an RC filter requiring at least 9 time constants for 12-bit settling.
Total conversion time equals sampling time plus 12 SAR cycles; input signal bandwidth is strictly limited by the Nyquist frequency (F_sample / 2).
ADC sequences support Regular round-robin scanning and high-priority Injected channel triggers with hardware End of Conversion (EOC) and Overrun (OVR) flags.
The internal V_REFINT bandgap channel allows firmware to dynamically measure power supply voltage (VDDA) droop and calibrate sensor measurements.

projectStep.title: Construct an Impedance-Calibrated Multi-Channel ADC Acquisition Engine with VREFINT Compensation
steps: Implement a 12-bit SAR binary search model and derive LSB quantization metrics for standard reference voltages.
Calculate RC time constants and sampling cycle requirements for high-impedance (50k–100k) analog sensors.
Calculate total conversion time budgets and establish anti-aliasing filter cutoffs according to Nyquist limits.
Configure a multi-channel regular sequence with EOC and OVR overrun detection flags.
Implement runtime power supply voltage calibration using internal V_REFINT and factory calibration constants.
